text:
Arun: seeing a reproducible p95/p99 latency spike on kv-heavy long-context workloads after the kernel-selector change from yesterday. load tests + canary show bursts of 300-500ms extra per-request.

Lina: saw that too in staging traces, looks correlated with high reinsert activity in the kv layer.

Marta: do we have a flame/trace? I want to see where time is going (paging vs CPU).

Arun: uploading the short trace and profiler output: https://internal/trace/2045678901 and run log below:
```
[2024-11-17T01:12:03Z] evict: policy=FIFO pressure=0.87 active_kv_entries=1.2M reinsert_ops=430 batch_size=16
[2024-11-17T01:12:03Z] page_scan: scanned_pages=1024 reclaimed=12 scan_time_ms=34
[2024-11-17T01:12:03Z] reinsert: key=0x7f8e... reinserts=7 chain_len=7 latency_ms=28
```

Devin: interesting — profiler shows a spike in "kv_reinsert.walk" and in the batching queue stall path. attaching a small visual: flame shows big stack in `kv::evict_reinsert` then in `batcher::await_slot`.

InfraBot: deploy-bot detected runtime rollout 2024-11-16T22:45 UTC => git@redwood/runtime@b3d9c4f (kernel-selector heuristics). No other infra changes.

Kenneth: hypothesis: kernel-selector picked the narrower-kernel path which reduces per-token CPU but increases short-lived allocation patterns? That could increase reinsert churn and cause FIFO to flip order under pressure.

Lina: code pointer — FIFO reinserts currently append to tail without updating reuse indices. Under bursts, a reinserted entry can be evicted again quickly, producing a cascade. LRU would bump reuse timestamp and avoid immediate eviction.

Marta: do we have correctness concerns (stale KV being served) or purely latency?

Arun: so far only latency/regression. I ran a correctness check: values returned match ground truth in tests. Problem is eviction/reinsert churn causing batch stalls and extra page scans.

Devin: repro steps I used locally:
```
# run the long-context loadgen with high concurrency
./tools/loadgen --profile kv --model gptx-large --seq 16k --concurrency 64 --duration 10m
# capture kv stats
./tools/kv-stats --interval 10s > kv-stats.log
```
Result: `kv_reinsert_rate` jumps from ~4/s to 450/s and p99 latency jumps.

Kenneth: I tried toggling policy to LRU on a canary host, p99 dropped back near baseline. So this looks like a policy interaction with reinserts.

Lina: note: FIFO has a cheaper eviction decision but cheaper doesn't help if it thrashes under bursty reuse. We might need a hybrid: FIFO for steady-state but LRU-bump when reinsert_count > N or when reinserted within T ms.

Marta: quick mitigation options:
- revert kernel-selector roll to avoid the allocation pattern change (fast rollback)
- add safety cap: limit per-request reinsert_count to 2 and track metric `kv_reinsert_capped`
- flip canary hosts to LRU policy for 1h and observe

Arun: I pushed a short patch that caps reinserts (PR: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/789). It adds `--kv-reinsert-cap=2` with default unset.

Devin: ran canary with cap=2 on staging for 30m: reinsert_rate dropped 10x, p99 improved ~220ms -> 30ms. No correctness alerts.

InfraBot: canary report: 3 hosts running runtime@b3d9c4f with kv-reinsert-cap=2. Health: ok.

Marta: next actions:
- (ASAP) schedule rollback if cap doesn't hold under prod load.
- (24h) instrument and emit `kv_reinsert_chain_len` histogram, `kv_reinsert_rate`, and per-policy eviction qlen.
- (48h) prototype hybrid policy (FIFO with bump-on-reinsert) in a feature branch.

Kenneth: I'll own the hybrid prototype. Lina, can you add the histograms + alerts?

Lina: sure — will add metrics and an alert if `kv_reinsert_rate > 50/s per-host` or `kv_reinsert_chain_len > 4` for >2 consecutive mins.

Arun: summary for SRE: cause = reinsertion churn interacting badly with FIFO (policy correctness okay but performance degenerates). mitigation = cap reinserts + canary LRU. long-term = hybrid policy + better telemetry.

sre-oncall: thanks — putting a pager rule temporarily to notify on the new metrics. keep updates in this thread. :+1:

Marta: FYI leaving notes for postmortem template: reproduction script, flame links, PRs, canary results. I'll start a short follow-up doc.

Arun: thanks team. I'll post a small follow-up in #eng-runtime when we have hybrid results.

Lina: tagging for visibility: @sre-oncall @infra-team @eng-runtime
